title: U.S. House · New Jersey's 10th District
area: Parts of Essex, Hudson, and Union counties, including most of Newark, East Orange, Irvington, Elizabeth, and Jersey City.

context.text: LaMonica McIver won the Democratic primary on June 2, 2026, defeating Lawrence Poster. Carmen Bucco won the Republican primary unopposed. Both advance to the November 3, 2026 general election, which is uncontested by any third-party or independent candidates.

summary.text: LaMonica McIver is the Democratic incumbent for New Jersey's 10th Congressional District. A Newark native and former educator and administrator, she served on the Newark City Council from 2018 to 2024, including as Council President, and was first elected to the House in a September 2024 special election to succeed the late Rep. Donald Payne Jr. She sits on the Homeland Security and Small Business committees. She faces a federal case over a May 2025 visit to a Newark ICE detention facility, in which she is charged with assaulting, resisting, impeding and interfering with federal officials and has pleaded not guilty.

background.text: Born in Newark, New Jersey, in 1986. Her official biography says she was born and raised in Newark's Central Ward, attended Newark public schools, and still lives there with her family.
Earned a bachelor's degree in English literature from Bloomfield College in 2008 and a graduate degree in education leadership, management and policy from Seton Hall University in 2011.

Worked for many years in education administration, most recently as Executive Director of the Essex Regional Educational Services Commission. She told Ballotpedia in 2024 that she had since moved to a private-sector role as a regional public affairs manager.
Founded Newark G.A.L.S., Inc. in 2012, an organization focused on developing female leaders.
Elected to the Newark City Council (Central Ward) in 2018 as the youngest woman ever to serve on the council, and served as Council President from 2022 to 2024.

Elected to the U.S. House in a September 2024 special election to complete the term of the late Rep. Donald M. Payne Jr., becoming the first Black woman to represent NJ-10, and won a full term in November 2024.

In the House, serves on the Homeland Security and Small Business committees, co-chairs the Caucus on Black Women and Girls, and is a member of the Congressional Progressive Caucus and the Congressional Black Caucus.

Was charged in May 2025 after a congressional oversight visit to Newark's Delaney Hall ICE detention facility and later indicted on three counts of assaulting, resisting, impeding and interfering with federal officials. She pleaded not guilty; in August 2026 a divided Third Circuit panel ruled she is not immune from prosecution, and she said the court got it wrong.
Her official biography says she is a mother of two and gave birth to a second daughter in 2026.

priorities.text: Addressing the interconnected challenges of affordability, housing, healthcare and education costs, and the local impact of climate change, including flooding in the district.
Securing safe, affordable housing, including policies to increase affordable housing options, protect tenants' rights, and address housing discrimination.
Combatting food insecurity through stronger nutrition assistance programs and access to nutritious food.
Gun violence prevention measures including universal background checks, closing background-check loopholes, and waiting periods.

positions.summary: Supports stricter gun laws, including universal background checks, closing loopholes in the background-check system, and waiting periods, calling gun violence a public health crisis.
Says she will always stand for protecting a woman's right to choose.
positions.quote: I will always stand for protecting a woman’s right to choose, for every American to have access to the ballot box, and to live without fear of violence.

positions.summary: Supports policies to increase affordable housing options, protect tenants' rights, and address housing discrimination.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Homeland Security (Subcommittees on Cybersecurity and Infrastructure, and Transportation and Maritime Security) and the House Committee on Small Business (Subcommittees on Economic Growth, Tax, and Capital Access; Innovation, Entrepreneurship, and Workforce Development; and Oversight, Investigations, and Regulations) in the 119th Congress.

On May 19, 2025, the interim U.S. Attorney for the District of New Jersey announced federal assault charges against McIver under 18 U.S.C. § 111(a)(1), stemming from a May 9, 2025 visit by McIver and other officials to the Delaney Hall ICE detention facility in Newark, during which Newark Mayor Ras Baraka was arrested (charges against Baraka were later dropped).

candidates.name: Carmen Bucco
candidates.ballotNote: Won the June 2, 2026 Republican primary unopposed

summary.text: Carmen Bucco is the Republican nominee for New Jersey's 10th Congressional District. He owns Bucco Couture, a tailoring business, and says he grew up in the foster care system. He was the Republican nominee for NJ-10 in 2024 and ran unsuccessfully for New Jersey State Senate District 20 in 2023 and General Assembly District 20 in 2025. His campaign website says he is running to put people first and focus on stopping corruption.

background.text: Born in New Jersey and graduated from Nutley High School in 1990.
According to his campaign website, he grew up in the foster care system and lived on the streets at times.
Works as a tailor and owns Bucco Couture, a tailoring business; his campaign website calls it a small business.
His campaign website says he has a foundation, Bucco's Rising Stars, that supports children.
Ran unsuccessfully as the Republican candidate for New Jersey State Senate District 20 in 2023, losing to incumbent Joseph Cryan.
Won the Republican nomination for NJ-10 and lost both the September 2024 special election and the November 2024 general election to LaMonica McIver.

Won the June 2025 Republican primary for New Jersey General Assembly District 20 with 95.2% of the vote and finished third in the November general election with 14.3%, behind Democrats Annette Quijano and Ed Rodriguez.
Won the June 2, 2026 Republican primary for NJ-10 unopposed.

priorities.text: Supporting law enforcement and first responders, and opposing policies he describes as "tying the hands of law enforcement."
priorities.quote: Tying the hands of law enforcement only endangers our way of life. We must always support our police and first responders and need to be tough on violent crimes while focusing on keeping our communities safe.

priorities.text: Reducing taxes and government spending, saying current policies are "driving inflation and impeding our quality of life."
priorities.quote: The policies of today are driving inflation and impeding our quality of life. We need to control our spending at the state level and stop frivolous spending.

priorities.text: Making it easier for small businesses to grow.
priorities.quote: We need to really hear what these businesses are going through and find solutions to make it easier for them to grow.

candidates.researchNotes: His campaign issues page (carmenbucco.com/issues) appears to date from an earlier campaign (it refers to running for 'State Congress, District 20') and states general themes; it does not take a side on the listed issues beyond saying he supports the Second Amendment. No 2026 questionnaire or interview answers found.

researchNotes: Ballot-access and candidate-slate facts drawn from Ballotpedia; not independently cross-checked against the NJ Division of Elections. Congress.gov and govtrack.us were unreachable in this environment, so a full list of bills McIver has sponsored in the 119th Congress could not be independently verified; per research guidance, her federal floor votes and FEC finance totals are added separately by script. Carmen Bucco has not completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey; his 2026-specific positions could not be found beyond his general campaign-site issues page (some content dates to a prior 2024 State Senate run) and his research depth is marked basic. McIver pleaded not guilty and a Third Circuit panel ruled in August 2026 that she is not immune from prosecution; a current trial date was not confirmed. Bucco's biography rests on Ballotpedia and his campaign site; no news profile was found.
